primarySourceInputs.observedPattern: Software-engineering agent trajectories preserve thought, action, observation, state, and query records for every step.
primarySourceInputs.localAbsorption: OpenClaude records the interrupted observation, recovery action, and final verification as parseable local JSONL trace events.

primarySourceInputs.observedPattern: Agent failure diagnosis normalizes raw logs, checks invariants, and emits auditable violation evidence before root-cause classification.
primarySourceInputs.localAbsorption: OpenClaude records a tool_observation_truncated_json invariant violation and bounded reread recovery before trusting the tool result.

primarySourceInputs.observedPattern: Outcome-only benchmark results hide where an agent failed; trajectory diagnosis should expose mechanism-level stages.
primarySourceInputs.localAbsorption: OpenClaude labels exploration, orchestration, implementation, and verification phases in the interruption-recovery trace.

primarySourceInputs.observedPattern: Passing outcomes can hide low-quality processes such as blind retries, missing verification, and disordered execution.
primarySourceInputs.localAbsorption: OpenClaude makes recovery explicit and requires final verification so the passing trace is inspectable as process evidence.

traceChecks.label: operator authorization is bounded to local no-provider trace capture
interrupted tool output was detected before trust
one invariant violation is recorded for the interrupted observation
recovery rereads the bounded fixture and writes fixture-only summary
trace contains failed interruption and succeeded terminal recovery
traceChecks.detail: started -> started -> succeeded -> failed -> succeeded -> succeeded -> succeeded -> succeeded -> succeeded

traceChecks.label: trace events are enriched with event names and trace context
all required process phases are represented
no provider live model or external calls occurred

claimBoundary: Tool-interruption recovery trace capture is local no-provider fixture evidence only. It does not call providers, live models, external services, mutate protected repositories, publish, deploy, launch, or authorize release, production, public, external-validation, benchmark-superiority, or autonomous-reliability claims.
